title: Failed cover-quality saves roll back to the wrong value
reasoning: updateCoverQuality computes rollback from the requested value instead of the previous UI/server value. For example, if the current quality is low and the user selects high, a non-409 update failure rolls the UI back to medium, not low. That leaves the settings screen showing a value that neither the user successfully saved nor the server currently has.
reproduction: Set coverQuality to low, make ghostwriterRepository.updateConfig return a non-409 Error while calling updateCoverQuality("high"), and observe the final UI state becomes medium.
recommendation: Capture the previous SettingsUiState before applying the optimistic update and restore that value on failure, or refetch server config for all update failures where the authoritative state is uncertain.
whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: No linked tests were provided, and a repo search found no tests covering SettingsViewModel cover config rollback behavior.
suggestedRegressionTest: Add a SettingsViewModel test that starts with coverQuality low, makes updateConfig fail, calls updateCoverQuality("high"), and asserts coverQuality is still low with an error message.
minimumFixScope: SettingsViewModel.updateCoverQuality and the rollback contract in updateGhostwriterConfig.
